question: According to National Multidimensional Poverty Index 2021, which of the following states recorded the steepest decline in poor?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Bihar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• According to the **National Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI) 2021**, Bihar showed the steepest decline in multidimensional poverty among all Indian states.
 
• The poverty rate in Bihar fell from **51.9% in 2015-16 to 33.8% in 2019-21**, a reduction of 18.1 percentage points.
 
• Approximately 13.01 crore people in India were lifted out of multidimensional poverty during this period, with Bihar making a significant contribution.
 
• Bihar achieved this progress through improvements in access to basic amenities such as **education, nutrition, housing, and sanitation.**
 
• Despite this achievement, Bihar remains among the states with the **highest levels of multidimensional poverty**, alongside Uttar Pradesh and Jharkhand.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Andhra Pradesh:**

 
 
• Andhra Pradesh has shown improvements in multidimensional poverty indicators, especially in sectors like education and health.
 
• Key schemes like **Nadu-Nedu** (focused on school infrastructure) and **YSR Aarogyasri** (health insurance) contributed to better outcomes.
 
 
 
• **Gujarat:**
 
 
• Gujarat has a relatively low poverty rate and has performed well in improving infrastructure and industrial growth.
 
• Initiatives like **SAUNI Yojana** (irrigation) and **urban development projects** helped improve living standards.
 
 
 
• **Maharashtra:**
 
 
• Maharashtra also recorded progress in reducing multidimensional poverty, with significant contributions from urban areas.
 
• Programs such as **Jal Jeevan Mission** and skill development initiatives have improved access to drinking water and employment opportunities.
 
 
 
• **National Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI):**
 
 
• The MPI measures poverty beyond income levels, focusing on factors like health, education, and living standards.
 
• It was developed by the **Oxford Poverty and Human Development Initiative (OPHI)** and adopted in India by **NITI Aayog**.
 
• Indicators include nutrition, child mortality, schooling, sanitation, drinking water, electricity, and housing.
 
• The MPI provides policymakers with data to assess the effectiveness of welfare schemes and identify areas needing targeted intervention.
